title: Characterization of an Ultrathin RuO2 Film/TiO2 Interface by Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: Ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) thin films have shown novel strain-modulated properties such as altermagnetism and superconductivity, which could be applied in developing spintronics and next-generation electronics [1, 2]. For example, ultra-thin, strained RuO2 films can be grown epitaxially on TiO2 substrates. For a film that is only a few unit cells thick, understanding the interface structure and its corresponding properties becomes increasingly critical, with few techniques available to probe their structure and defects.
